title: appsci-bench evaluation dataset
description: A task's held-out eval dataset for the evaluator: a turn type, run controls, and the list of EvalSamples. The samples may be stored inline (data) or, in the task spec, under a directory pointed at by evaluation_data.dataset -- one subdirectory per data_point_id, each holding a sample.json (this $defs/eval_sample shape) plus any files it references by file_path. See docs/evaluator_system_design.md (Datasets).

type.description: single_turn = one query per sample; multi_turn = the artifact agent user sim drives a conversation.

max_turns.description: Max turns the artifact agent gets during user simulation (multi_turn).

repeat.description: How many times each data point is rerun for stability (scores averaged across repeats).

max_steps.description: Shared simulation-step budget for multi_turn data; replaces max_turns. Each speaker message costs one step and each individual tool request/result costs two.

allOf.$comment: Exactly one of file_data / file_path -- catches a sample that gives neither or both.

file_data.description: base64-encoded bytes, inline. Use for small files; for large ones prefer file_path.

file_path.description: Path to the file's bytes, relative to this sample's own eval_data/<data_point_id>/ directory (never repo-root). Alternative to inline file_data -- the loader (appsci_bench/eval/dataset.py) resolves it at load time and reads the bytes lazily, on first use. Dataset-authoring convenience only: the wire protocol (/query_session) always carries real file_data, never a path.

artifact_agent_io.description: ArtifactAgentQuery / ArtifactAgentOutput: any of text, json, files.

user_stop_criteria.default: The user task has been successfully completed.

name.description: The tool's name, exactly as the environment's tool route takes it. This is also what authorises a call: the sim may only call a tool this case grants.

description.description: What the tool does, in one line. Rendered into the simulator's prompt so it can tell which of its tools fits the moment.

parameters.description: The tool's JSON-Schema parameter object, exactly as an OpenAI-style function declares it: {"type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}. The simulator is told each argument's name and whether it is required. Absent or empty means the tool takes no arguments, which the prompt states outright.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for a tool whose signature this dataset does not carry: the name alone. The prompt still lists it, but the simulator cannot fill its arguments -- see the array description.

user_tools.description: Tools the SIMULATED USER holds and may call during the conversation (the customer's own capabilities, e.g. submitting an application themselves). Optional; absent or empty means the user only talks, which is the behaviour for every task that does not model user-side actions. The eval-time sim can EXECUTE one only when the run supplies an executor (see task_runner.env_tool_token_var) -- but it can only fill a tool's ARGUMENTS from the signature declared here, and its instructions forbid inventing values. So a tool given as a bare name is effectively callable only if it takes no arguments: any case whose golden outcome needs a customer-side action on a tool with arguments will fail for a reason unrelated to the artifact. Declare the full object for those. NOTE the signature duplicates what the environment's own toolkit defines, so it can drift; a task declaring signatures should assert the two agree (see banking's test_user_tool_schemas.py).

expected_output.description: Optional per-sample structured ground truth / params for the eval functions. Objectives are task-level (no per-sample objective spec), so anything that varies per sample lives here: put structured data in its `json` field (a JSON-encoded string), e.g. {"required_actions": [...]} for an airline trajectory check. The eval function parses it and owns the comparison semantics.

eval_rubric.description: Optional per-sample natural-language description of what success looks like, for LLM-judge-style eval functions to read. NL text only -- put structured params in expected_output.json, not here. This is per-DATA-POINT and varies sample to sample -- it is NOT where a metric's own scoring criteria goes; that is authored once by the task designer and belongs baked into that metric's own eval function/prompt, fixed for every sample.
